records.title: Because for simple reasons
records.objective: Give a direct reason with because.

concept.en: Use because before a clause that gives the reason for something.
concept.vi: Dùng because trước một mệnh đề để nêu lý do trực tiếp cho một việc.

whenToUse: Give a simple reason for an action, feeling or situation.

positive: I stayed home because I was tired.
We are happy because the test is easy.
Because it is raining, we need umbrellas.

variations: Because introduces the reason; so introduces the result.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Present Continuous: temporary situations

concept.en: Use the Present Continuous for temporary situations happening around the present time, even if not happening this exact second.
concept.vi: Dùng Hiện tại tiếp diễn cho tình huống tạm thời đang diễn ra trong khoảng thời gian hiện tại, dù không nhất thiết đúng ngay giây đang nói.

whenToUse: Describe a temporary living, working or study situation.
Talk about a short-term change around now.

positive: I am staying with my aunt this week.
Leo is working from home this month.
They are taking a short course this summer.

variations: Temporary Present Continuous contrasts with Present Simple for usual or permanent situations.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Present Simple vs Present Continuous: basic contrast

concept.en: Use the Present Simple for routines, facts and states; use the Present Continuous for actions happening now or temporary situations.
concept.vi: Dùng Hiện tại đơn cho thói quen, sự thật và trạng thái; dùng Hiện tại tiếp diễn cho hành động đang xảy ra hoặc tình huống tạm thời.

whenToUse: Choose between a usual action and an action happening now.
Contrast a regular situation with a temporary one.

positive: I usually take the bus, but today I am walking.
She works in Hanoi, but this month she is working in Da Nang.

variations: State verbs such as know and like usually use the Present Simple, not the Present Continuous.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Was/were
records.objective: Describe past states, identity and location.

concept.en: Use was with I/he/she/it and were with you/we/they to talk about past states, identity and location.
concept.vi: Dùng was với I/he/she/it và were với you/we/they để nói về trạng thái, danh tính hoặc vị trí trong quá khứ.

whenToUse: Describe where someone was in the past.
Describe a past state or condition.

positive: I was at home yesterday.
They were tired after the trip.
Was she at school this morning?

variations: Negative forms are was not/wasn't and were not/weren't.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Past Simple: regular verbs
records.objective: Form and use regular past verbs for finished events.

concept.en: Use the Past Simple of regular verbs, usually formed with -ed, for finished actions in the past.
concept.vi: Dùng Quá khứ đơn của động từ có quy tắc, thường thêm -ed, cho hành động đã kết thúc trong quá khứ.

whenToUse: Talk about a finished action yesterday, last week or at another finished past time.
Tell simple past events in sequence.

positive: We visited the museum yesterday.
She cleaned her room last night.
They played football after school.

variations: Spelling changes include live → lived, study → studied and stop → stopped.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Past Simple: common irregular verbs
records.objective: Use high-frequency irregular past forms in finished events.

concept.en: Some common verbs have irregular Past Simple forms that do not use -ed, such as go → went and see → saw.
concept.vi: Một số động từ thông dụng có dạng Quá khứ đơn bất quy tắc không thêm -ed, như go → went và see → saw.

whenToUse: Talk about finished past events with common irregular verbs.
Describe simple past experiences and actions.

positive: We went to the park.
I saw an old friend.
She had breakfast at seven.

variations: Learn high-frequency irregular forms as fixed verb pairs: go/went, see/saw, have/had, get/got.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Past Simple: negatives and questions
records.objective: Use didn't + base verb and Did...?

concept.en: Use did not/didn't + base verb for Past Simple negatives and Did + subject + base verb for questions.
concept.vi: Dùng did not/didn't + động từ nguyên mẫu cho câu phủ định Quá khứ đơn và Did + chủ ngữ + động từ nguyên mẫu cho câu hỏi.

whenToUse: Say that a past action did not happen.
Ask whether a past action happened.

positive: I didn't call yesterday.
Did she finish the book?
Did they go by bus?

variations: After did or didn't, use the base form: did go, didn't see, not did went or didn't saw.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Be going to: intentions and plans
records.objective: Talk about plans and intentions already decided.

concept.en: Use be going to + base verb for a future plan or intention that is already decided.
concept.vi: Dùng be going to + động từ nguyên mẫu cho kế hoạch hoặc ý định tương lai đã được quyết định.

formulae: Subject + am/is/are going to + base verb.
whenToUse: Talk about a personal plan already decided.
Say what someone intends to do soon.

positive: I am going to study tonight.
She is going to visit her aunt.
We are going to cook at home.

variations: Use the correct form of be before going to: am/is/are.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.
